subject: roller coaster
title: A Doctor Took a Fake Kidney on a Roller Coaster 20 Times. It Worked

scenes.text: A patient passed kidney stones on a roller coaster. Three times in a row.
So urologist David Wartinger 3D-printed a clear kidney, filled it with urine and three small stones.
He packed it in a backpack and rode Big Thunder Mountain at Disney World twenty times.
Sitting in the back car, about sixty-four percent of the stones came out. In the front, about seventeen percent.
Why? The back car gets the sharpest jolts and drops, shaking small stones loose.
Bigger rides worked worse. And yes, it won an Ig Nobel Prize.

description:
Michigan State urologist David Wartinger took a 3D-printed silicone kidney model with small stones on Disney's Big Thunder Mountain Railroad 20 times; about 64% of stones passed in the rear car versus about 17% in the front (Journal of the American Osteopathic Association, 2016).
The model study, preliminary and not done on patients, won the 2018 Ig Nobel Prize in Medicine.
Front row or back row?
first_comment: Space Mountain, with bigger drops, worked less well. Are you a front-car or back-car rider?
